# clean tree and any NEW disagreement stands out.

# "It has always been like that" is not one -- num.m had always been like that
# too, and it was a bug for five months.

column3: octavefemm wraps the call as print(ci_readdxf(...)), byte-identical to FEMM 4.2's mfile. Under OF's Lua that echoed the result to the console; here it means the wire returns nothing instead of the result. Inherited, not introduced -- but worth revisiting, since the other four bindings return the value.

column1: # --- octavefemm-only convenience aliases, absent elsewhere by design ---
# The `2` suffix forms take a point pair where the base form takes coordinates.
# They are octavefemm idiom and were never ported; the base command is present
# *_getview renders the view to a temporary file and reads it back, so each
# binding invents its own random filename. The argument can never match, and
# octavefemm additionally implements the whole thing via *_savebitmap.

column3: temp filename is randomly generated per call; octavefemm routes via ci_savebitmap

column1: # --- wrappers whose arguments are ARRAYS, which the contract cannot express ---
# The contract derives arity and string-vs-number from octavefemm's sentinels;
# it has no way to say "this argument is a vector". juliafemm types its
# signatures, so it rejects the scalar sentinels outright rather than emitting
# something wrong. Layer 2 is what will cover these.

column3: takes vectors (a B-H table); the contract cannot express an array argument

column1: # The engine accepts create() and newdocument() as the same command; verified

column1: # --- benign: the engine treats a missing flag as "show" ---
# octavefemm's *_shownames() takes no arguments and hardcodes the flag as 1;
# pyfemm's takes *arg and passes through, so with no arguments it sends
# *_shownames() with no flag. gui/main.cpp:386 and :431 both read
# `nargs == 0 || args[0] != 0`, so no flag means show -- identical behaviour.
# --- bulk getters, implemented differently by design ---
# octavefemm builds eo_getallelements client-side from straccum/strappend over
# the scalar getter (4 commands); everyone else calls a single C++ bulk getter.
# Same data, different number of commands. See docs/bulk-getters-design.md.

column3: octavefemm composes it from 4 commands; the others send one
